mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.22 in the current month
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not revert below 0.22 within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor market strength above 150,000 jobs signals resilient wage growth, which elevates expected corporate profits and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns over the 60-day window average no more than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or PAYEMS falls below 145,000 for the next 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO supply index below 100 signals tight inventory conditions, which amplifies demand-side pressure and produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses below 101 in the current month
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX 5d returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or INDPRO re-expands above 105 within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST retail sales above 2% suggests resilient consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns, especially when UNRATE is below 3.5%.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2% AND UNRATE < 3.5 in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05) during the trigger period, or UNRATE rises above 3.5% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% for two consecutive months creates a forward discounting effect, compressing future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the two-month FEDFUNDS decline, or FEDFUNDS rises above 1.5% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS relative to GDPC1 (RSAFS/GDPC1 < 0.85) indicates softening demand for credit-sensitive assets, which amplifies risk aversion and drives negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 crosses below 0.85 in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns during the trigger window are not statistically negative (Rank IC > 0.05), or the ratio reverts above 0.85 within 15 days.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in GDPC1 GDP growth below -0.5% suggests a softening economy, which elevates risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns, especially when INDPRO is above 105.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -0.5 AND INDPRO > 105 in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns during the trigger are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or GDPC1 recovers ≥ 0.5% within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a tightening cycle is signaled by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% while UNRATE remains below 4%, which increases real interest expectations and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5 AND UNRATE < 4 in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns during the trigger are not statistically negative (Rank IC > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS falls ≤ 4.5% within 30 days.
